clauses.requirement: Stop lamps of categories S1, S2, S3, S4 and MS shall comply with the specific technical requirements of UN R148 paragraph 5.5.
The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied of the stop lamp shall meet the luminous intensity and standard light distribution requirements in Table 7 (UN R148 para 5.5.1).

Stop lamp luminous intensities shall meet Table 7 (minimum luminous intensity per para 4.8.3.1(d); maximum for a single lamp per 4.8.3.1(a); maximum for a lamp marked 'D' per 3.3.2.5.2 per 4.8.3.1(b); standard light distribution per 4.8.3.1(c)): S1 steady min 60 cd, max 260 cd single, 130 cd marked D, Figure A3-I; S2 min 60 cd, max 730 cd single, 365 cd marked D, variable 60 cd day, 7 cd night, Figure A3-I; S3 steady min 25 cd, max 110 cd single, 55 cd marked D, Figure A3-III; S4 min 25 cd, max 160 cd single, 80 cd marked D, variable, Figure A3-III; MS steady min 40 cd, max 260 cd single, 130 cd marked D, Figure A3-I; angles of geometric visibility per Table A2-1; minimum luminous intensity within the angles of visibility 3E-1 of the on-axis minimum (day) and 7E-2 (night) as listed in Table 7.
The minimum luminous intensity of the stop lamp within the angles of geometric visibility shall meet the values given in Table 7.
There are no requirements for the minimum or maximum area of apparent surface of stop lamps.
Measurement of stop lamps shall be performed in accordance with the provisions of paragraph 5.5.4 and its sub-paragraphs.

For a category S3 or S4 stop lamp intended to be mounted inside the vehicle, the colorimetric characteristics shall be verified with the worst-case combination(s) of lamp and rear window(s) or sample plate(s).
For a stop lamp pair (MS), the standard light distribution may, at the request of the applicant, be considered from the VV line to the outboard side only.
